correctness.rationale: The determinant-one graph-potential coordinate transformation exactly enumerates all constraints. Fubini plus symmetric moving-slab differentiation give the section where min(v)-max(u)>=h-1; its beta integral is a!b!/(d-1)! (3-h)^(d-1). The anchored undeformed baseline is a direct range-density beta integral. Integrating gives the stated continuous all-parameter identity including endpoints by continuity. Totally unimodular difference constraints justify Ehrhart leading coefficients; 33 integer and six rational-height exact-arithmetic finite checks reproduce the formula but are not used in place of the proof. Normalization, h endpoints, and p,q>=2 boundaries were checked.

value.rationale: The problem measures exact geometric sensitivity of the natural Lipschitz dual Banach ball when one metric edge becomes redundant. The result solves the full parameter and dimension family, proves an exact dimension-dependent high-order cancellation at h=3, and determines a sharp balanced-versus-unbalanced relative edge-deletion response. This is not merely an existing h=1 normalization or arbitrary isolated finite computation; it describes the structural transition from active to redundant metric constraints and can benchmark perturbation geometry.
